A1.what: Ready lane kit (shared helpers, facts pack, cheat sheet)
A1.body: The helpers should be geometric ops that compute from the scene, not typed helpers (S1). The facts pack is generated: `make_lane_brief.py` fills the 25-plus `{{...}}` fields from `metrics.yaml`, `inventory.yaml`, `services.yaml` and `brief.yaml`. The cheat sheet becomes a Blender 5.x gotchas file plus tool cards (applicable cases, constraints, known failures) for each builder, as SceneWeaver does (SceneWeaver). A new `lane-builder` agent (Opus, preloads `house-rules`, fix-lane text, `linear-runs`; live tools and `Agent` disallowed; a Stop-hook check that `report.json` and the replay evidence exist) replaces the `modeler` as the fix-lane agent (orch §6, §8.13)

A2.body: Add the mechanism: item cap, planned minutes, hard stop, `progress.json`, `maxTurns` (S2). Agents are time-blind and effort-blind, so the budget goes in the brief (Carlini; Anthropic multi-agent); SceneWeaver capped itself at 10 iterations with memory length 1. In BlenderWorld, turns per task ranged from 45.6 to 158 across models and more image views did not raise the score (BlenderWorld), which supports code over repeated looking

A3.what: Cut start-up context (MCP allowlist, slimmer preloads)
A3.body: One estimate may be wrong. Measured: preloads and listings are 10-25k of a 70-100k start; the other 20-40k is an estimate for tool and MCP schemas (orch §2A). But Claude Code defers MCP tool definitions by default, so only names and server instructions enter context (costs docs), and the schema share may be small. First action: `/context` inside one lane agent and record `start_tokens`. Then: `tools`, `mcpServers` and `disallowedTools: Agent` on all 11 agents (none sets them); preload diet (blender-worker 16.0k, modeler 8.0k, supervisor 7.3k times four); load the stage skill named in the brief on demand
A3.gain: Medium-high (8-20k per spawn measured from preloads)
A3.status: `adopt_now` the measurement and preload diet; `test_first` the allowlist

A4.what: Whole-scene lint with in-frame items first
A4.body: The likely cause of piled-up defects is a text contradiction (Q2), not only the missing whole-scene run. Keep the `new` gate for speed and add a total-per-class ratchet and a gate-close sweep, as SonarQube does for new against overall code and as Epic's whole-project Validate Data does (S3)

A5.body: Write the exit criteria down: `gates.yaml` and `check_gate.py` (required files, lint state, reviews present, tasks closed, board fields, the frozen-lighting path to G3), severity-banded, with the bar narrowing by round (all, then blockers and majors, then blockers only). No studio publishes a "done" definition, so it must be measurable (game §1; qa Key Question 2; Mullich; Lemon Sky). Where G2 stops: a proxy-grade blockout (silhouette, proportions, material groups: Amazon) is the common stop, but `detail: detailed` builds features in the blockout, against `level-design`'s "dress after play" (build §1). Which stop the user wants is part of D5
A5.status: `adopt_now` `gates.yaml`; the stop point is the user's call

A6.body: `check_brief.py` fails on leftover `{{`, unknown material names (against the gate file), duplicate ID prefixes, missing seam owners, objects absent from the gate copy and items over the cap; `fix_issues.schema.json` validates the 12 optional keys; house rule 10 is "enforced by: none" today (orch §2E). The delegation brief carries objective, output format, tool guidance, boundaries and caps, and the agent returns a file path plus a short summary (Anthropic multi-agent)

A7.what: Shift checks left, never hand-fix live
A7.body: Add a fixer-versus-report split: lint `--fix` for names, tags, origin and scale (mechanical, reversible, logged in the ledger), report-only for budgets, density and form (LightspeedLA lists a fixer framework as a future direction; the vendor split is a claim). Add rollback on regression (P4), a `.live.lock` plus a PreToolUse hook on `execute_blender_code` that checks the agent type (orch §6), and `check_targets.py` for "check a number before you hand it over" (`supervisor:88`)

A8.what: Thin manager with planned handoffs and a SessionStart compact hook
A8.body: Write `plan/STATE.md` (stage, gate, round, open fix IDs, running agents, locked decisions, next three actions, under 60 lines), `agents.json`, `tasks.yaml` (a user note cannot close without evidence) and `decisions.yaml`. A `SessionStart` hook with the `compact` matcher injects a short factual digest, `PreCompact` rewrites `STATE.md`, and the memory-only rules move into `house-rules` (Q18). Root `CLAUDE.md` is re-injected after compaction but rules given only in conversation are summarised away, and skills re-attach only their first 5,000 tokens each, so critical text goes first (memory docs; hooks; skills). Manager hygiene: never `cat` `lint.json`, reviews or reports; final messages at most 15 lines plus paths; a fresh manager session at each gate. Anthropic's harness lets workers flip only a status field in a JSON ledger (harnesses)
A8.gain: High: survives 23 compactions in 8.7 h; user notes cannot be dropped

A9.body: `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop` and `PreCompact` hooks append to `plan/telemetry.jsonl`; `retro_numbers.py` reads the main and `subagents/*.jsonl` transcripts, `steps.json` and `reviews/*`; a rate card feeds planned minutes; a `Monitor` watchdog alerts at 1.5 times plan. Track first-pass approval and rounds per issue as health signals and keep the original estimates for the retro (Lemon Sky; Scrum.org). Telemetry also settles the effort and model questions with data (orch §8.7)

P4.what: Rollback on regression: after a step, compare lint and metrics with the previous backup and revert automatically if worse; never overwrite the best state

P5.what: A reviewer protocol: six oblique RGB views plus the reference crop, numeric measurements and camera pose in the prompt, one criterion per call, shuffled candidate order, and lint as the only gate for contact and missing-part claims; consensus polling and a golden-image diff outside the fix region as tests

P8.what: Model and effort tiering as an experiment: run one lane or reviewer one tier lower on the same items and compare lint and replay results
P8.status: `test_first`; never a default (detail over cost; D8)
